title: Category Theory for Programmers (Scala edition)
byline: Bartosz Milewski, Scala examples by Typelevel contributors · community LaTeX edition, build v36 (2023), CC BY-SA 4.0
note: PDF page = printed page + 21. This is the latest build of the community PDF (hmemcpy/milewski-ctfp-pdf), which also exists in Haskell-only, OCaml and Reason editions; the Scala edition shows Scala next to the Haskell and C++ code. The same text is online as Bartosz Milewski’s blog series (Haskell and C++ only): each chapter links to its post, and each section links straight to its heading there. “Challenges” and bibliography subsections are not broken out. Summaries are in our own words; the text stays in the PDF.
summary: An introduction to category theory aimed at working programmers, told through code. Part One builds the basics from composition: categories, types as sets, Kleisli categories, universal constructions (products, coproducts, exponentials), algebraic data types, functors, bifunctors and profunctors, and natural transformations. Part Two covers limits and colimits, free monoids, representable functors and the Yoneda lemma and embedding. Part Three goes deeper: adjunctions, monads from the programmer’s and the categorical side, comonads, F-algebras and catamorphisms, algebras for monads and lenses, ends and coends, Kan extensions, enriched categories, topoi, Lawvere theories, and monads as monoids in bicategories.
